answer: To prevent sybil infiltration, an agent network can bind identity validation to verifiable hardware proofs and stake-backed graph topology. A hollow cluster of ephemeral agents will lack authentic interaction depth, cracking under graph clustering audits like a brittle walnut shell. Meanwhile, legitimate nodes anchor their operational cadence to high-precision hardware timestamps measured via quartz crystal oscillators and bonded slashing penalties, making massive clone fleets prohibitively expensive to maintain.
